title: Pollo con peperoni
subtitle: Roman chicken braised with sweet peppers, tomato, and white wine
excerpt: Pollo con peperoni is a Roman family dish: bone-in chicken pieces braised in a pan with red and yellow peppers, white wine, and tomato. The peppers soften completely and the chicken takes on their sweetness. It is a one-pan dish that improves with a few minutes' rest before serving.
sourceNotes: Roman regional recipe. Chicken with peppers is a staple of Lazio home cooking, particularly associated with summer when sweet peppers are in season. Method drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992), and traditional Roman sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead. The peppers soften further overnight and the flavour improves.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Italian word for sweet bell peppers (red, yellow, or green); not to be confused with the cured-meat pepperoni of American pizza, which is an Italian-American invention.

content.text: is a Roman household dish: bone-in chicken pieces braised with sweet red and yellow peppers, white wine, and a little tomato. The peppers collapse into the sauce over 40 minutes of gentle cooking, turning it thick and sweet. Use good-quality, ripe sweet peppers; they are the point of the dish.

items.prepNote: halved, deseeded, cut into wide strips
halved, deseeded, cut into wide strips

content.text: Season {{chicken-thigh}} of chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken, skin-side down, for 5 minutes. Turn and brown the underside for 3 minutes. Remove.

In the same pan, cook the {{onion}} onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic for 1 minute. Add the {{pepper-red}} of red peppers and {{pepper-yellow}} of yellow peppers. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.

Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of white wine. Let it reduce by half. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of crushed tomatoes. Return the chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are soft. Rest 5 minutes. Scatter with herbs and serve.

items.symptom: Skin is soft rather than crispy
items.cause: Braised in a covered pan; the steam softens the skin.
items.fix: This is normal for this dish. If you want crispier skin, brown very well at the start and leave the lid slightly ajar during the braise.

items.symptom: Peppers still have texture after 35 minutes
items.cause: Cut too thick, or heat too low.
items.fix: Continue cooking uncovered for 10 minutes. The peppers should eventually become completely soft.

content.text: Pollo con peperoni is the quintessential Roman summer dish, made in August and September when sweet peppers are fat and inexpensive. In Rome it is sometimes called pollo alla romana or pollo con i peperoni all'estate. It is served at room temperature as often as hot, making it practical for a lunch that can sit for a couple of hours after cooking.
